newsitem.title: KENYA: Relatives greet survivors of Ethiopia air crash.
newsitem.headline: Relatives greet survivors of Ethiopia air crash.

text.p: Relatives greeted loved ones they feared were dead in the Kenyan capital on Monday after a hijacked Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 767 crashed into the sea off the Comoros Islands.

Twenty-nine injured survivors, including nine stretcher cases, arrived in Nairobi by air and were taken to Nairobi Hospital, Ethiopian Airlines officials said. A total of 52 of the 175 passengers and crew aboard the plane survived, according to Ethiopian Airlines' main office in Addis Ababa.
There were scenes of joy and relief at Nairobi airport.

"I am so happy that it turned out this way. When I heard the news that the plane had crashed I thought no one would have made it," said Efrem Asmellash, an Ethiopian whose 61-year-old father was a passenger.

"Then somebody called me from (the Comoros capital) Moroni and said my father was alive and it was only then I started to have hope," said Asmellah, adding he had mixed feelings about a crash in which so many had died.
Asmellah's father Sebhatu, whose left shoulder was injured when the plane hit the water, said he survived after freeing himself and swimming to the shore.
Other survivors told how they swam ashore after struggling to get out of the downed plane.

As many as 51 missing bodies could be trapped in the wreckage, officials said. The plane broke into three pieces when it crashed into the sea just off the shoreline of the main island of the Indian Ocean archipelago on Saturday after running out of fuel.
